stories.title: Nepal floods: 469 killed almost 1,000 still missing
stories.summary: A lake formed by a landslide on the Nepal-China border started to overflow, triggering panic and putting at risk areas devastated by a flash flood two days ago as rescue efforts were briefly halted. Wednesday's catastrophic ⁠flood caused by a glacier collapse killed 489 people in Nepal and five in China-controlled Tibet, with almost 1,000 more missing in the two countries. Of those missing, at least 540 are foreign nationals, including two Irish citizens, who have been named by the Nepalese Tourism Department as 46-year-old Santosh Sahu and 18-year-old Spandan Sahu. The Department of Foreign Affairs said in a statement that it "continues to closely monitor the situation following serious flooding in Nepal and, together with partners, is working to account for two Irish citizens visiting the area."

stories.title: Vhi to increase prices by average of 2.75% from October
stories.summary: Vhi is to increase the prices of its health insurance policies by an average of 2.75% from the beginning of October. This will be the provider's second price rise this year, after it announced a 3% average hike across its plans that took effect in March. Vhi is the largest health insurance company in Ireland, with around 1.2 million customers - roughly half of the entire market. The latest increases will see the price of its EnhancedCare 250 plan, which is especially popular among young adults, go up by €22 a year to €1,300 for an adult.

stories.summary: Senior officials from the Departments of Transport and Justice, as well as gardaí, the Road Safety Authority and Transport Infrastructure Ireland, are to meet on Friday to discuss motorway road safety. The meeting at Leinster House follows a number of recent incidents on the country's motorway network and will be hosted by the Minister of State with responsibility for Road Safety Seán Canney. In a statement, Mr Canney said he wanted to bring key road safety partners together to discuss what can be done to improve safety on motorways. Mr Canney said it is "a complex issue which has many causes" and that it will "not be easily solved".

stories.title: Stripe, Advent consortium said to drop pursuit of PayPal
stories.summary: A consortium of payment processor Stripe and buyout firm Advent has decided to abandon its pursuit of fintech pioneer PayPal, Bloomberg News has reported, citing people familiar with the matter. PayPal, Stripe and Advent declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The payments company, once the crown jewel of American financial technology, received a $60.50-per-share bid from Stripe and private equity firm Advent International, which valued it at more than $53 billion, Reuters reported in July, citing sources. The offer is a fraction of the roughly $360 billion valuation PayPal commanded as a pandemic-era darling in 2021.

stories.summary: Mike Solan is set to become the next manager of the Offaly footballers after being proposed by the Faithful County's management committee. Solan, who left his position as Longford boss earlier this month, will go forward for ratification at September’s county board meeting. If accepted, he will begin a three-year term and will be joined in the management team by former Mayo, Sligo and Longford coach Joe Keane and Offaly legend Nigel Dunne, who guided the Faithful minors to Leinster glory for the first time in 35 years in 2025. As well as Longford, Solan has previously managed the Mayo Under-21s and was part of Andy Moran’s management team in Leitrim.

The Insolvency and Companies Court, a specialist court within the High Court, deals with bankruptcy petitions.

stories.title: Leinster to keep Spicer despite guilty plea for assault
stories.summary: Leinster Rugby has confirmed that second row Alan Spicer remains a member of the province's academy for this season, but he has been disciplined internally after appearing in court charged with assaulting a woman earlier this year. In June, the 21-year-old lock avoided jail time and a criminal conviction after he pleaded guilty to assault causing harm of a woman in her 20s, in an incident at Copper Face Jacks nightclub in Dublin on 1 March. Spicer paid €10,000 in compensation to the victim, who suffered dental injuries when he flicked a plastic cup into her face during an altercation. The former Ireland U20 international has not played for the province since his arrest in March.

stories.title: Slí na Samhlaíochta - celebrating the legacy of Manchán Magan
stories.summary: Musical Director Simon O'Reilly introduces Slí na Samhlaíochta/The Way of Imagination, a live performance coming to the National Concert Hall this October that brings together spoken word, music, and visual art in an exploration of the concept of Tír na nÓg through the work of the late author, traveller, broadcaster and documentary maker Manchán Magan. Slí na Samhlaíochta began at the Hedge School Festival in Doolin in 2023, an event I co-founded to bring musicians, writers and visual artists together to create new work. For the closing performance, Manchán Magan brought a spoken-word piece inspired by Tír na nÓg and An Saol Eile, the Otherworld of Irish tradition. Myles O'Reilly and I created a live score around his words, while Crosby Dunkley developed the visuals that accompanied the performance. None of us expected the response. From the opening moments there was a stillness in the room that is difficult to describe. The audience seemed completely immersed and, afterwards, many spoke about how deeply they had been affected. I came away feeling we had created something that deserved another life.

stories.title: 7 ways to minimise dark circles at home
stories.summary: Dark circles are one of the most prolific skin concerns across all ages, and can be down to a myriad of reasons ranging from alcohol to hormones to lack of sleep or simply genetics. "Dark circles are slightly misleading because they are not really one condition," explains aesthetic practitioner Dr David Jack. "What we perceive as darkness underneath the eyes can come from increased melanin in the skin, visible blood vessels through very thin eyelid skin, changes in the underlying anatomy that create shadow or sometimes a mixture of all three." The colour can offer some indication of the cause. Jack says brownish circles are more suggestive of pigmentation, while blue, purple or reddish tones can indicate a greater vascular component.

stories.title: Gas demand increases by 5% in July from June
stories.summary:
New figures from Gas Networks Ireland show that overall gas demand in Ireland increased by 5% in July on the previous month. July was the second hottest July since records began and one of the sunniest on record, but the warm and sunny weather was accompanied by periods of low wind conditions, which meant a lower supply of wind energy.

Against this backdrop, demand for gas for the electricity generation sector increased by 10% on a monthly basis, while gas demand from almost all other industry sectors fell during the month.

Today's figures show that gas accounted for 43% of the country's electricity generation in July, up from 40% in June. They also reveal that gas generation peaked at 70% during the month and never fell below 21%. Meanwhile, wind accounted for 22% of electricity generation, down from 30% in June. Solar accounted for another 9%.

Gas Networks Ireland's Director of Regulation and Strategy, Edwina Nyhan, said the July figures demonstrate the important role gas continues to play in Ireland’s energy system.

stories.title: Hundreds killed, nearly 1,000 missing after Nepal floods
stories.summary: Rescuers searched Himalayan valleys and hillsides after a flash flood that killed at least 389 people and left nearly 1,000 missing, as Nepal and China warned of a risk of fresh flooding from water pooling in two lakes. Both countries said a glacier collapse sent a huge torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris cascading through Himalayan mountain river systems, sweeping through villages and key infrastructure down a route thronged by trekkers and pilgrims that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Chinese-controlled Tibet. Authorities in Nepal used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off in towns and valleys, while emergency services recovered dozens of bodies swept down into the plains. stories.title: Dublin Fringe: How do you turn Kafka into a show for children?
stories.summary: Theatre Lovett take a joyful journey into the world of Franz Kafka for the Dublin Fringe Festival this September, with their latest family show, Kafka's Doll - Louis Lovett introduces a tale of love and loss, packed with songs, music, circus, juggling, puppetry, unicycling... and a pinch of magic. Franz Kafka is famous for dark, strange and sometimes bewildering stories. So how on earth does Theatre Lovett turn Kafka into a show for children and families? Kafka loved jokes, games and laughter. His fiancée Dora remembered that he "made everything into a game" and that they laughed together all the time. He was also a great storyteller and entertainer. When Kafka once read The Trial aloud to friends before it was published, they reportedly laughed so much that Kafka himself had to stop reading. It is this playful, mischievous side of Kafka that inspired our new work, Kafka’s Doll.

stories.title: Mater to compensate employee for racial discrimination
stories.summary: One of the country's largest hospitals has been ordered to pay €10,000 compensation for racially discriminating against a Nigerian-born employee when suspending him primarily based on the colour of his skin. At the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) adjudicator, Penelope McGrath BL ordered Mater Misericordiae University Hospital to pay €10,000 compensation to healthcare assistant, Paul Agbons for discriminating against him on the grounds of race when suspending him for six days from 6-12 June last year. In making the award, Ms McGrath stated that the employer had to balance two very difficult situations and that she was mindful of the fact that the suspension only lasted six days. On 13 June 2025, the hospital told Mr Agbons "that he did not have a case to answer" arising from the patient's complaint.

stories.title: More EU nationals declaring themselves bankrupt here
stories.summary: The trend of EU nationals establishing their centre of interest here in order to declare themselves bankrupt accelerated in 2025. That is according to the 2025 annual report by the Insolvency Service of Ireland (ISI) which shows that of the 85 individuals to declare themselves bankrupt here in 2025, 37 involved debtors originating from other EU member states "and the vast majority from Germany, with all their debt situated outside Ireland". Bankruptcy here usually lasts one year and the report shows that the 85 to declare themselves bankrupt last year was a 20% increase on the 71 to declare themselves bankrupt here in 2024. The EU nationals accounted for 43.5% of bankruptcies in 2025, compared with 25% in 2024.

stories.title: LOI preview: Chasing pack look to put pressure on Rovers
stories.summary: With league leaders Shamrock Rovers not in action until Sunday due to their unsuccessful exploits in Europe, the chasing pack have the opportunity to cut the gap at the top. With the Hoops travelling to Derry on Sunday, both second-placed St Patrick's Athletic and Bohemians in third will be looking to reel in the defending champions. The Saints host a resurgent Waterford who are on a seven-game unbeaten run, a streak that has allowed them to move clear of the relegation zone, while Bohemians host bottom side Sligo Rovers. The Bit O’Red are without a league win since May and running out of games to avoid relegation. Elsewhere there’s a mid-table clash between Shelbourne and Galway United, with both sides looking for a win that could help them force their way into the European conversation.

stories.title: Sligo reshuffle management as Sloyan takes sole charge
stories.summary: Sligo have reshuffled their managerial deck ahead of the 2027 season with last year's joint-managers Dessie Sloyan and Eamonn O'Hara pivoting into a manager-assistant manager arrangement. Sloyan will be the man in charge with Yeats County legend O'Hara becoming his assistant. The pair were joint-managers for just one season but the county have moved to make the adjustment ahead of the 2027 campaign. A statement from Sligo Co Board read: "At a meeting of its County Committee last evening (Monday, 24 August 2026) Sligo GAA endorsed the management teams for its senior football and hurling and U20 football teams for 2027.
